native_result.query: The effect of which variable on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024 to 0.0923 (while becoming insignifcant) when both SES and academic characteristics are included in analysis?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of SES on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636  (significant) to  -0.2293 (insignificant) and effect of race on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024  (significant) to 0.0923 (insignificant) when academic characteristics are considered.
native_result.HypoB: RACE (SAMPLE_RACE) is the variable whose effect on BA degree completion decreases to ~0.0923 and becomes insignificant when both SES and academic characteristics (ASVAB ability composite and percentile in class) are included: the White-vs-non-White log-odds coefficient falls from a significant positive value in the bivariate model to -0.0926 (p=0.68, 95% CI [-0.53, 0.35]) in the full model, indicating that racial differences in BA completion are largely accounted for by socioeconomic status and academic preparation.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Inspected data (8,773 rows, 8 variables, 0 missing; outcome 236/8,537). 2) For each candidate X in {SES, ABILITY, PCTCLASS, FAMSIZ, RACE, SEX}, fit nested logistic regressions: Model A = BA ~ X; Model B = BA ~ X + SES + ABILITY + PCTCLASS; compared X's coefficient, p-value, and 95% CI. 3) Identified RACE (White contrast) as the unique match to the cited 0.0923 full-model coefficient that becomes insignificant (p=0.68 > 0.05). 4) Sensitivity: OLS linear-probability models show the same attenuation pattern; grid search over all covariate subsets confirmed {SES, ABILITY, PCTCLASS} uniquely reproduces the cited full-model coefficient.
